prompt: Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with knee injury after a hit while turning left. The patient had 28 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1409; do not mention it.)
text: The patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck from the side while the patient was turning left. The patient reported immediate pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion in the right knee, with difficulty bearing weight in the first days after the incident. Initial examination showed effusion, medial joint line tenderness, and pain with valgus stress. Imaging was obtained to rule out fracture, and no acute bony injury was identified. The working assessment was a medial collateral ligament sprain with associated meniscal irritation. Treatment consisted of a structured course of physical therapy focusing on quadriceps strengthening, gait retraining, and progressive range-of-motion exercises, combined with activity modification and anti-inflammatory medication as needed. Over 28 visits, the patient demonstrated steady improvement in swelling, pain scores, and functional tolerance for stairs and prolonged standing. At the most recent evaluation, the patient had nearly full range of motion with mild residual discomfort on deep squatting. Continued home exercise and periodic reassessment are recommended, with return to full activity anticipated as strength and stability are maintained.
